note: No AI features, so no ai_* labels. No committed .env, .dev.vars or wrangler.jsonc (all gitignored). Example files hold empty values or placeholders, and a secret-pattern grep of the whole repo found only placeholder connection strings. All 15 tables enable RLS with no policies, so the anon key gets nothing through the Supabase REST API. App data goes through server-side Drizzle. All 44 data server fns carry authMiddleware (getAuthStatus checks the session itself), and every id-based read, update and delete checked also filters by the session user_id. No service-role key in client code. Cron routes check a shared secret with a constant-time compare. Tesla tokens are AES-GCM encrypted at rest. No fake actions or mock data found in the app. Test fixtures stay in *.test.ts. components/ui/* skipped as vendored shadcn. Not reviewed: scripts/import-tessie.mjs, merge-charges.mjs and the converter and reconcile scripts beyond grep, *.test.ts files, and most dashboard route pages and view-model files beyond grep.

labels.what: Supabase URL and anon key read from VITE_ env and shipped to the browser for login. Public by design. Every table has RLS on with no policies

The app is meant for one owner, but the middleware accepts any Supabase user and has no owner allowlist. Blocking new accounts depends on a manual Supabase setting (README step 2). Every id lookup filters by user_id, so a second account cannot read the owner's data. The risk is cost: a new account can link its own Tesla and the cron poller will poll it on the owner's Fleet API credit
The author's real VIN, home charging site name and country, and charging receipt numbers with dates and amounts are committed to a public repo as importer input
Importer defaults are tied to the author's setup: receipts file path, UTC+8 offset (480) and an assumed 7 kW charger. All can be overridden by CLI flags
Raw database and Tesla API error text is returned to the browser (resync result message, getAuthStatus error at line 37, and up to 300 characters of the callback error in the redirect URL)
PACK_KWH = 75 is still the fallback pack size for drive energy when the vehicle row has no pack_kwh, so drive energy is wrong for other pack sizes
Default charging loss factor 1.1 is repeated as a literal in rate.functions.ts, cost.ts, drive-detail.functions.ts line 204, RateForm.tsx line 39 and schema.ts line 299
Default home radius 150 m is repeated as a literal in geo.ts, rate.functions.ts, geofences.functions.ts (validator and seedHomeGeofence), RateForm.tsx line 43 and schema.ts lines 305 and 373

The home radius has two different caps: saveRate allows up to 5000 m, the geofence form allows up to 20000 m, and marking a geofence as home writes its radius into electricity_rate.home_radius_m (geofences.functions.ts line 94). The same value is valid on one path and rejected on the other
USD is the hardcoded fallback currency in about 15 places across UI and server code, while the author's own data is in MYR
RECONCILE_CRON '0 * * * *' is hardcoded in code and must match the cron string in wrangler config. If they drift, the hourly reconcile silently becomes another poll run
Public OpenStreetMap tile server URL hardcoded in two map components (and openfreemap and AWS terrain URLs in ReplayMap3D.tsx lines 18-20). OSM tile policy limits heavy use
Default signing proxy URL https://localhost:4443, overridable with --proxy
MQTT broker allows anonymous clients. It is safe only while docker-compose keeps port 1883 unpublished
fleet-telemetry uses the unpinned :latest image and runs as root on public port 443
